channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India sign package of documents to strengthen partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and India signed a series of bilateral documents following high-level talks between President Mirziyoyev and Prime Minister Modi. The agreements aim to deepen cooperation in trade, investment, culture, education, environmental protection, and tourism.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Modi awarded Uzbekistan's highest state order
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Damodardas Modi has been awarded the Order of "Oliy Darajali Doʻstlik" of Uzbekistan. The award recognizes his significant contributions to strengthening Uzbek-Indian friendship, strategic partnership, and multifaceted cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan's 35 years: Path to open dialogue between state and society
item.description: Uzbekistan's journey over 35 years of independence is marked by progress towards open dialogue between the state and society. Media pluralism has expanded, with changes in public communication and the media's role in state-society interaction, though legal frameworks predate recent reforms.

item.title: China and Kyrgyzstan strengthen transport links and cooperation within the SCO framework
item.description: China and Kyrgyzstan are actively developing transport infrastructure, including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project and the Bedel border crossing. Chinese President Xi Jinping highlighted these efforts in an article, emphasizing their role in promoting regional connectivity and mutual benefit within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi awarded the Order of Friendship of the Highest Degree in Uzbekistan
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was awarded the Order of Friendship of the Highest Degree at the Kuksaroy residence. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented the award, stating it signifies the high esteem of the Uzbek people and state for Modi's contributions to strengthening historical friendship between the two nations.

item.title: Bishkek mayor promises aid to victims of 'Madina' market fire
item.description: The mayor of Bishkek met with traders at the 'Madina' market following a fire, promising assistance to those affected. Authorities will identify victims and provide support, ensuring safety and allowing the fire to be extinguished. The cause is under investigation, with preliminary findings suggesting an electrical short circuit.

item.title: Uzbekistan collected over 3 trillion soms via IMEI device registration system
item.description: Uzbekistan has collected over 3 trillion soms through its IMEI device registration system. Officials warn that abolishing the payment system would ultimately harm the state budget. The Telecommunication Networks Management Republican Center reported this information.

item.title: Chinese workers in Bishkek to be relocated after mass brawl, 20 deported
item.description: Chinese citizens working in Bishkek will be relocated following a mass brawl at their dormitory. The conflict involved foreign workers, leading to the detention of 20 individuals who will be deported from Kyrgyzstan. Preparations are underway to move the workers to new accommodations.

item.title: Kyrgyz economist: Gulf investment potential not fully utilized
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has a strong political foundation for relations with Gulf countries, but practical investment cooperation needs expansion. An economist noted that while political dialogue is established, translating it into concrete commercial projects remains a challenge. The full potential for attracting capital from Gulf states is not yet realized, despite significant foreign investment.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi awarded Uzbekistan's Order of Friendship
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was awarded Uzbekistan's Order of High Friendship at the Kuksaroy residence. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented the award for Modi's contribution to strengthening historical friendship ties. The leaders agreed to elevate bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership, discussing cooperation in political, economic, and cultural spheres.

item.title: Three emergency workers injured fighting Madina market fire in Bishkek
item.description: Three emergency workers were injured while extinguishing a large fire at the Madina market in Bishkek. Two received outpatient treatment, while one was taken to the toxicology department; their conditions are moderate. The fire, which spread over a thousand square meters, was localized. Preliminary cause is suspected to be a short circuit.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping accorded ceremonial welcome in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan were ceremonially welcomed at Manas International Airport in Kyrgyzstan. They were greeted by President Sader Japarov and his wife, with national flags, a red carpet, and a guard of honor. Traditional Kyrgyz performances and gifts were presented.

item.title: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister: SCO is a center for forming a multipolar world order
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev stated that the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) is becoming a key center for forming a multipolar world order. He emphasized that the SCO is not directed against anyone and offers a platform for equal dialogue and mutual respect.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India agree to boost trade to $5 billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have agreed to increase bilateral trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030. The agreement was reached during talks between Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Tashkent. Discussions also covered elevating cooperation to a comprehensive strategic partnership level, focusing on trade, economy, investment, and humanitarian ties.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India agree to increase mutual trade to $5 billion by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have agreed to elevate their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership and increase mutual trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030. The agreement was reached during talks between Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Bilateral trade exceeded $1 billion last year, with sevenfold growth in joint ventures.

item.title: Two firefighters injured while extinguishing fire at 'Madina' market in Bishkek
item.description: Two firefighters sustained minor injuries while battling a large fire at the 'Madina' market in Bishkek. Their condition is stable. The fire, which spread over an area exceeding one thousand square meters, was localized. The preliminary cause is suspected to be a short circuit.

item.title: Nepal Flood Death Toll Rises to 734, Identification Challenges Persist
item.description: The death toll from floods in Nepal has reached 734, with the high number of victims and bodies washed hundreds of kilometers posing significant identification challenges. Additionally, 2,498 people are missing, including 589 foreign nationals. The extensive flooding has caused widespread destruction and displacement.

item.title: Tashkent Schools to Use AI to Analyze Student Behavior and Psychological State
item.description: Tashkent schools will implement an AI system to analyze student behavior and psychological states to prevent juvenile delinquency. This initiative follows a reported increase in crimes committed by minors, despite an overall decrease in youth crime in Uzbekistan. The "Smart School" system will install cameras in classrooms of grades 9-11.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi Received with State Ceremony in Tashkent
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was accorded a ceremonial welcome at the Kuksaroy residence during his state visit to Uzbekistan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev greeted the guest, after which national flags were raised and an honor guard was inspected. The leaders then proceeded to high-level negotiations.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi Received with State Ceremony in Tashkent
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was accorded a ceremonial welcome at the Kuksaroy residence during his state visit to Uzbekistan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev greeted the guest, after which national flags were raised and an honor guard was inspected. The leaders then proceeded to high-level negotiations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Citizens' Travel to Turkey Increased by 17.7% Year-on-Year
item.description: In January-July of this year, over 166,000 citizens of Uzbekistan traveled to Turkey. This figure represents a 17.7% increase compared to the same period last year, indicating a rise in travel between the two countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan offers food aid and reconstruction support to Palestine
item.description: Kazakhstan has expressed readiness to provide practical assistance to the Palestinian people, including food aid and participation in the reconstruction of Gaza's social infrastructure. Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Issagaliyev stated Kazakhstan's support for a political resolution to the conflict based on the "two states for two peoples" principle.

item.title: China-Nepal Border Landslide: 16 Dead, 546 Missing; Climate Change Cited
item.description: A landslide on the China-Nepal border has resulted in 16 deaths and 546 missing persons. Experts attribute the disaster to glacier instability caused by long-term climate warming. Chinese authorities have allocated over $30 million for rescue efforts, with over 2,000 rescuers on site. 261 foreign nationals are among the missing.

item.title: Fire at Bishkek's 'Madina' Market Localized Over 400 Square Meters
item.description: A fire at the 'Madina' market in Bishkek has been localized, affecting approximately 400 square meters. Emergency services are working to extinguish remaining hotspots in containers. The preliminary cause is suspected to be a short circuit.

item.title: All Bishkek Fire Trucks Deployed to Combat 'Madina' Market Blaze
item.description: All available fire trucks in Bishkek were deployed to fight a large fire at the 'Madina' market. The fire, which started in a container and spread to stalls, is believed to have been caused by a short circuit. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Dengue Fever Cases Surge 85% in Afghanistan, WHO Reports
item.description: The World Health Organization reports an 85% increase in dengue fever cases in Afghanistan. The surge, along with rises in coronavirus and other infectious diseases, is straining the country's healthcare system due to seasonal outbreaks and shortages of medicine and resources.

item.title: US woman kills child to prevent father gaining custody
item.description: A woman in the United States has killed her child to prevent the father from gaining custody. The mother was reportedly unhappy about the father being granted parental rights and had previously abducted the child.

item.title: Afghanistan border crossing closures reduce Pakistan-Tajikistan trade by 70%
item.description: The closure of Afghanistan's border crossings has led to a nearly 70% reduction in trade between Pakistan and Tajikistan. Exports from Pakistan to Tajikistan fell by 61.3% to $11.9 million, while imports decreased by 82.8% to $3.3 million.

item.title: SCO Summit in 2026 to Emphasize 'Shanghai Spirit' Amid Global Transformation
item.description: The 2026 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit will focus on the 'Shanghai Spirit'—mutual trust, benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity, and common development—amidst global changes, unilateralism, and bloc confrontation. The SCO emphasizes non-alignment and resolving disputes through dialogue, countering terrorism and cyber threats.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan at 35: Reflecting on independence, responsibility, and personal growth
item.description: As Kyrgyzstan marks 35 years of independence, the author reflects on the nation's journey, comparing it to reaching an age where personal responsibility replaces blaming external circumstances. The piece explores freedom, accountability, and the realization of potential.

item.title: Nazarali Aripov Appointed Kyrgyzstan's Ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Nazarali Aripov has been appointed as the new Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Tajikistan. President Sadyr Japarov signed the decree. Aripov previously served as Consul General in Almaty from May 2021 to June 2024. He replaces Erlan Abdyldaev, who was ambassador since April 2022.

item.title: Kazakhstan Schools Face Overcrowding with 380,000 First-Graders
item.description: Kazakhstan's schools are preparing for over 380,000 first-graders this academic year, raising concerns about class sizes and teacher workload. An Almaty teacher noted that large classes hinder individual attention and teaching quality, advocating for classes of 12-15 students.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank maintains interest rate amid inflation concerns
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank has kept its key interest rate at 12 percent due to external instability and geopolitical conflicts impacting the domestic market. Inflation has reached 7.3 percent year-to-date, with food prices up 6.3 percent. The bank aims to curb inflation by maintaining tight monetary conditions.

item.title: US to cut off Egypt's second-largest bank from global finance system
item.description: The Trump administration is set to disconnect Banque Misr, Egypt's second-largest bank, from the global financial system as part of new measures to increase financial pressure on Iran and its allies. The bank's UAE branch will be unable to conduct US dollar transactions once sanctions take effect.

item.title: Global media highlights Bishkek's role in upcoming SCO summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: International media is focusing on Bishkek ahead of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit and the World Nomad Games. Outlets like AFP view the SCO as a counterweight to Western influence, while others analyze regional dynamics and Kyrgyzstan's ambition to host major international events.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister arrives in Uzbekistan for state visit
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan for a state visit at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. He was welcomed at Tashkent-Humo International Airport by the Uzbek President. State flags and an honor guard were present for the occasion.

item.title: Chinese magazine features Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary
item.description: A special issue of China's 'Luokai' magazine highlights Uzbekistan's 35th independence anniversary, detailing reforms and achievements in politics, economy, and culture. It covers bilateral cooperation, investment potential, the Islamic Civilization Center, and the 'Uzbekistan-2030' strategy.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India's Strategic Partnership Shows Growing Momentum
item.description: Uzbek-Indian relations have gained new momentum since 2017, evolving beyond political dialogue to multifaceted practical cooperation. This strategic partnership spans politics, economy, industry, health, digital sectors, education, security, and transport, driven by political will and complementary economies.

item.title: Russia's Foreign Ministry Calls Armenia's Mobilization Statements a Provocation
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova labeled statements by Armenian Security Council Secretary Alen Simonyan regarding accepting Russians in case of mobilization as a provocation. Zakharova stated Simonyan's remarks encourage illegal actions and politicize Armenian hospitality. The ministry expressed regret over Yerevan's public statements undermining bilateral cooperation with Moscow.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents Parliamentary Diplomacy Experience at Phnom Penh Conference
item.description: Uzbekistan shared its parliamentary diplomacy experience at the II Inter-Parliamentary Conference in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. The delegation highlighted the strengthening atmosphere of good neighborliness and cooperation in Central Asia, emphasizing constructive dialogue for conflict resolution.
